---
title: Adjustment clips
description: Grade everything behind a clip in one place, over a range, a selection or the whole timeline, and set how strongly the grade applies.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An adjustment clip has no picture of its own. For as long as it lasts, it grades everything already drawn behind it, so one grade can cover a whole scene, or a graphic that has no Color tab of its own.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip"
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Adjustment"
  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

<Shot
  name="05c-clip-adjustment.window"
  alt="The editor with a rose clip named Adjustment selected on its own track, above a video clip on the Video track. The inspector shows only the Color and Clip sub-tabs. Color opens on the Adjustment section with Strength at 75%, then the Qualifier section, which reads off."
/>

## What an adjustment clip is

An adjustment clip grades every lower track and the canvas background. It never touches a track in front of it, so a title above it stays as it is.

On the timeline it's a plain rose block with its name strip and action lane, and no filmstrip. It has no file behind it, so you can trim or move it freely to change what it covers.

## Insert an adjustment clip

<Steps>

1. Say what it should cover: set an [In/Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), or select the clips. With neither, it covers the whole timeline.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**. It has no shortcut.

3. Grade in the **Color** sub-tab, which is already open. The new clip is selected and the inspector shows **Clip ▸ Color**.

</Steps>

The whole thing is one undo step, **Add Adjustment Clip**. The menu item is greyed out while a nest is open, and when the timeline has nothing to cover.

### Its span

| What's set | What the new clip covers |
| --- | --- |
| An In/Out range | The range, even if clips are selected too |
| Selected clips, no range | From the first selected clip's start to the last one's end |
| Neither | The whole timeline |

### Its track

The new clip goes on the front track when that track has room for the whole span and isn't a matte track. Otherwise Frame Job adds a new front track named **Adjustment** and puts the clip there. A matte front track is never used, because an adjustment clip on one [does nothing](#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).

A project holds up to 64 tracks. If the front track has no room and there are no tracks to spare, nothing is added.

## The full grade

An adjustment clip's **Color** sub-tab has the same grade a picture clip has, plus two sections of its own at the top. In order:

| Section | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Adjustment** | [Strength](#strength), how much of the grade is applied |
| **Qualifier** | Narrows the grade to the pixels you pick. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). |
| [Light](/color/light/) | Exposure and tone |
| [Color](/color/color-section/) | Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue |
| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Balance shadows, middle and highlights |
| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Master, RGB and [hue curves](/color/hue-curves/) |
| [Look](/color/looks/) | A built-in look or a [.cube LUT](/color/luts/) |

**Adjustment** and **Qualifier** show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip. Select one alongside a picture clip and you get the shared grade sections without those two.

### No Picture tab

An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so it has no **Picture** sub-tab. Its sub-tabs are **Color** and **Clip**. **Picture** also disappears whenever any adjustment clip is part of the selection.

Placement, crop, corners, shadow, reflection and the like can still arrive on one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). They're kept and have no effect.

## Strength

**Strength** sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip. At 100 % you see the full grade, and at 0 % you see the picture as it was.

| Control | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Strength** | 0 to 100 %, in whole percent, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind the field's chevron | 100 % |

The section's header shows the current strength. Its **Reset** button returns to 100 %, as one undo step named **Adjustment**.

## Fade the grade in or out

An adjustment clip can't take a transition, so animate its Strength instead. Select an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) on the clip's action lane and change **Strength**. The value goes to the action's end, and the grade ramps there from the clip's own Strength. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Confine it to part of the picture

An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:

- **To an area:** put a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) directly in front of the adjustment clip's track. On a track cut by a matte, the clip grades only inside the matte. The matte cuts everything on that track, so keep other clips off it.
- **To a colour or brightness:** set a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/). It picks pixels by hue, saturation and luma.

The two work together. The grade reaches only the pixels both allow, mixed at the clip's Strength.

The adjustment clip must not sit on the matte track itself. There it has no effect, and the inspector says "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect."

## Grade a graphic

[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. Select the clip first and **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** matches its span. The adjustment clip grades every track behind it, so add a matte if other tracks show through.

## Limits

### No nests

An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.

To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.

### No transitions or overlaps

An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit and tells you to fade the clip instead, which you do with its [Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out). Two clips that only touch are fine.

### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes

These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.

The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.

## Good to know

- A clip with no grade set changes nothing, and neither does a qualifier on its own. A qualifier narrows a grade, so there has to be one.
- The [speed](/speed/overview/) commands and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed or left out for an adjustment clip, because it has no source and no picture size.

## With an agent

`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the track and at the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a duration. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.

`set_video` then grades it with everything the Color tab offers, and can also give it point filters directly. To an agent, Strength is the clip's opacity, and `set_action_end` animates it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**. It has no shortcut.

3. Grade in the **Color** sub-tab, which is already open. The new clip is selected and the inspector shows **Clip ▸ Color**.

</Steps>

The whole thing is one undo step, **Add Adjustment Clip**. The menu item is greyed out while a nest is open, and when the timeline has nothing to cover.

### Its span

| What's set | What the new clip covers |
| --- | --- |
| An In/Out range | The range, even if clips are selected too |
| Selected clips, no range | From the first selected clip's start to the last one's end |
| Neither | The whole timeline |

### Its track

The new clip goes on the front track when that track has room for the whole span and isn't a matte track. Otherwise Frame Job adds a new front track named **Adjustment** and puts the clip there. A matte front track is never used, because an adjustment clip on one [does nothing](#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).

A project holds up to 64 tracks. If the front track has no room and there are no tracks to spare, nothing is added.

## The full grade

An adjustment clip's **Color** sub-tab has the same grade a picture clip has, plus two sections of its own at the top. In order:

| Section | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Adjustment** | [Strength](#strength), how much of the grade is applied |
| **Qualifier** | Narrows the grade to the pixels you pick. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). |
| [Light](/color/light/) | Exposure and tone |
| [Color](/color/color-section/) | Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue |
| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Balance shadows, middle and highlights |
| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Master, RGB and [hue curves](/color/hue-curves/) |
| [Look](/color/looks/) | A built-in look or a [.cube LUT](/color/luts/) |

An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so it has no **Picture** sub-tab. Its sub-tabs are **Color** and **Clip**. **Picture** also disappears whenever any adjustment clip is part of the selection.

**Strength** sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip. At 100 % you see the full grade, and at 0 % you see the picture as it was.

| Control | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Strength** | 0 to 100 %, in whole percent, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind the field's chevron | 100 % |

An adjustment clip can't take a transition, so animate its Strength instead. Select an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) on the clip's action lane and change **Strength**. An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:

[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.

To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.

An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit and tells you to fade the clip instead, which you do with its [Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out). Two clips that only touch are fine.

### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes

These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.

The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.

- The [speed](/speed/overview/) commands and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed or left out for an adjustment clip, because it has no source and no picture size.

## With an agent

`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the track and at the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a duration. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.

## Related

- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)

---
title: Qualifiers
description: Limit an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels of one colour or brightness, using hue, saturation and luma ranges.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A qualifier limits an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/)'s grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma. Use it to change one colour and leave the rest of the picture alone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'render_frame']}
  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
/>

<Shot
  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
  alt="The Qualifier section of an adjustment clip, its header reading hue · sat. Hue is ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30°, Soft 15°, and Saturation at Low 0.15, High 1.00, Soft 0.05. Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
/>

## Grade one colour

<Steps>

1. Put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) above the picture, for the span you want.

2. Give it a grade in the **Color** sub-tab. A qualifier on its own changes nothing, because it only narrows a grade.

3. In the **Qualifier** section, press **Pick from Canvas** and click the colour in the preview. Or tick a range and set it by hand.

4. Tick **Show Selection** to see what's picked. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).

5. Adjust the ranges until the selection is clean, then untick **Show Selection**.

</Steps>

A qualifier reaches every track behind the clip. To keep it to one area as well, [add a matte](/color/adjustment-clips/#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).

## The Qualifier section

The **Qualifier** section appears only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip, right after **Adjustment**. A picture clip can't have a qualifier.

It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).

Matching reads the picture behind the clip as it was before the grade, so the grade never changes what it selects.

### The Qualifier summary

The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.

**Reset** appears once anything is set. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.

## Turn a range on

Each range has a checkbox, a strip and three fields. Tick the checkbox and the range starts at its default. That's one undo step named after the range, as unticking it is.

A range that's off has a dimmed strip that ignores presses, and greyed-out fields, so tick it first. Unticking forgets the range's values: tick it again and it's back at its default.

## The three ranges

| Range | Picks pixels by | Strip | Fields | Default when ticked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Hue** | Their colour | The colour spectrum, 0 to 360° | **Centre** 0 to 360°, **Width** 0 to 360°, **Soft** 0 to 180°, in whole degrees | Centre 30°, Width 50°, Soft 25° |
| **Saturation** | How colourful they are | Neutral to fully saturated | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
| **Luma** | How bright they are | Black to white | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |

A number typed outside a field's range is held at the nearest end of it.

### Hue range

**Centre** is the colour, and **Width** is how much of the spectrum around it is fully picked. **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. The default sits on skin tones: 5° to 55° is fully picked, fading to nothing at 340° and 80°.

The band wraps round the spectrum, so a range centred on red picks from both ends of the strip.

Greys are never picked by hue. A colour fades out of a hue range as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, on a scale of 0 to 1.

### Saturation range

This is HSV saturation: 0 is neutral and 1 is fully saturated. **Low** and **High** are the edges of what's fully picked, and **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. At its default the range passes everything, so it does nothing until you narrow it.

Near-black reads as 0, so dark noise doesn't count as colour. A range that starts above 0 leaves near-black pixels out.

### Luma range

This is brightness, from 0 for black to 1 for white, measured as Rec. 709 Y′. Its fields work as Saturation's do, and at its default it passes everything too.

### Low and High never cross

On **Saturation** and **Luma**, a typed **Low** is held at or below **High**, and a typed **High** at or above **Low**. Dragging stops at the same point.

## How ranges combine

A pixel has to fall inside every range that's on. Tick **Hue** and **Luma** and you get that colour at that brightness, not either one.

Each range falls off smoothly across its **Soft** value outside each edge. The partial amounts multiply, so a pixel in the soft edge of two ranges is graded less than one in the soft edge of either. **Soft** at 0 gives a hard edge.

## Use a strip

Each strip is a live picture of its range, and the quickest way to set it.

### Read a strip

A strip shows its own scale: the spectrum for Hue, a neutral to red ramp for Saturation, black to white for Luma. It's dimmed 60 % outside the range and 30 % across the soft bands, so what stays bright is what's fully picked.

The two block knobs mark the range's edges, and the two small squares mark where the softness runs out.

### Drag a strip

| Drag | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| A block knob | On Hue, the **Width**, evenly about the centre. On Saturation and Luma, the **Low** or **High** edge. |
| A small square | **Soft** |
| The band between the knobs | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps round. Saturation and Luma stop at the ends of the scale, keeping their width. |

A press within 5 points of a handle takes it, and knobs are taken before squares. When a range runs to the end of its scale, as Saturation and Luma do at their defaults, the square sits under the knob, so use the **Soft** field or narrow the range first.

A drag is one undo step, named after the range.

### Drag at a tenth of the speed

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move a handle at a tenth of the speed.

### Reset a range

Double-click a strip to put the range back to its default. It stays on. To turn it off, untick it, or right-click the row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Invert

Tick **Invert** to grade everything except what the ranges pick. It's off by default. Use it to desaturate everything but one colour, for example.

## Blur

**Blur** softens the selection, not the picture. On noisy footage a speckled selection turns clean, and the grade blends into its surroundings.

| Control | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Blur** | 0 to 100 %, a slider and a field with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind its chevron | 0 % |

At 100 % the blur is a Gaussian of 24 canvas pixels, and it scales with the canvas, so a Half or Quarter preview blurs the same share of the picture as an export. It's one undo step named **Qualifier Blur**.

Blur never softens a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip, and it does nothing while no range is on.

## Animate a qualifier

An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate a qualifier. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control: the change goes to the action's end, and the numbers ramp there from the clip's own values.

- **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur** ramp smoothly.
- The hue centre takes the short way round the spectrum, so 350° to 10° passes through 0°.
- A range turned on or off, and **Invert**, switch at the action's end.

While an action animates the qualifier, a strip's band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour. The action holds the qualifier as one setting, so changing any row marks them all. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Good to know

- With several adjustment clips selected, the section shows the first clip's values and a badge marks the rows that differ. A change sends the whole range to every selected clip.
- **Invert** with no range on grades nothing, because every pixel counts as picked and Invert takes them all away.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a qualifier only from one adjustment clip to another. A picture clip gets none, and an adjustment clip keeps its own when the attributes come from a picture clip.
- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the ranges are measured on the HLG signal and Luma uses BT.2020's weights, so pick them again after switching a project's dynamic range.

## With an agent

`set_video` sets a qualifier, and can change part of a range and leave the rest as it is. Where the inspector holds a typed number inside its range, an agent's number outside the bounds is turned away. A qualifier on anything but an adjustment clip is an error naming the clip.

`render_frame` can draw the picture [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) shows, for one adjustment clip, and `set_action_end` animates a qualifier. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/)
- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)

---
title: Adjustment clips
description: Grade everything behind a clip in one place, over a range, a selection or the whole timeline, and set how strongly the grade applies.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An adjustment clip has no picture of its own. For as long as it lasts, it grades everything already drawn behind it, so one grade can cover a whole scene, or a graphic that has no Color tab of its own.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip"
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Adjustment"
  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

<Shot
  name="05c-clip-adjustment.window"
  alt="The editor with a rose clip named Adjustment selected on its own track, above a video clip on the Video track. The inspector shows only the Color and Clip sub-tabs. Color opens on the Adjustment section with Strength at 75%, then the Qualifier section, which reads off."
/>

## What an adjustment clip is

An adjustment clip grades every lower track and the canvas background. It never touches a track in front of it, so a title above it stays as it is.

On the timeline it's a plain rose block with its name strip and action lane, and no filmstrip. It has no file behind it, so you can trim or move it freely to change what it covers.

## Insert an adjustment clip

<Steps>

1. Say what it should cover: set an [In/Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), or select the clips. With neither, it covers the whole timeline.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**. It has no shortcut.

3. Grade in the **Color** sub-tab, which is already open. The new clip is selected and the inspector shows **Clip ▸ Color**.

</Steps>

The whole thing is one undo step, **Add Adjustment Clip**. The menu item is greyed out while a nest is open, and when the timeline has nothing to cover.

### Its span

| What's set | What the new clip covers |
| --- | --- |
| An In/Out range | The range, even if clips are selected too |
| Selected clips, no range | From the first selected clip's start to the last one's end |
| Neither | The whole timeline |

### Its track

The new clip goes on the front track when that track has room for the whole span and isn't a matte track. Otherwise Frame Job adds a new front track named **Adjustment** and puts the clip there. A matte front track is never used, because an adjustment clip on one [does nothing](#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).

A project holds up to 64 tracks. If the front track has no room and there are no tracks to spare, nothing is added.

## The full grade

An adjustment clip's **Color** sub-tab has the same grade a picture clip has, plus two sections of its own at the top. In order:

| Section | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Adjustment** | [Strength](#strength), how much of the grade is applied |
| **Qualifier** | Narrows the grade to the pixels you pick. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). |
| [Light](/color/light/) | Exposure and tone |
| [Color](/color/color-section/) | Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue |
| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Balance shadows, middle and highlights |
| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Master, RGB and [hue curves](/color/hue-curves/) |
| [Look](/color/looks/) | A built-in look or a [.cube LUT](/color/luts/) |

**Adjustment** and **Qualifier** show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip. Select one alongside a picture clip and you get the shared grade sections without those two.

### No Picture tab

An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so it has no **Picture** sub-tab. Its sub-tabs are **Color** and **Clip**. **Picture** also disappears whenever any adjustment clip is part of the selection.

Placement, crop, corners, shadow, reflection and the like can still arrive on one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). They're kept and have no effect.

## Strength

**Strength** sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip. At 100 % you see the full grade, and at 0 % you see the picture as it was.

| Control | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Strength** | 0 to 100 %, in whole percent, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind the field's chevron | 100 % |

The section's header shows the current strength. Its **Reset** button returns to 100 %, as one undo step named **Adjustment**.

## Fade the grade in or out

An adjustment clip can't take a transition, so animate its Strength instead. Select an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) on the clip's action lane and change **Strength**. The value goes to the action's end, and the grade ramps there from the clip's own Strength. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Confine it to part of the picture

An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:

- **To an area:** put a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) directly in front of the adjustment clip's track. On a track cut by a matte, the clip grades only inside the matte. The matte cuts everything on that track, so keep other clips off it.
- **To a colour or brightness:** set a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/). It picks pixels by hue, saturation and luma.

The two work together. The grade reaches only the pixels both allow, mixed at the clip's Strength.

The adjustment clip must not sit on the matte track itself. There it has no effect, and the inspector says "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect."

## Grade a graphic

[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. Select the clip first and **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** matches its span. The adjustment clip grades every track behind it, so add a matte if other tracks show through.

## Limits

### No nests

An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.

To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.

### No transitions or overlaps

An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit and tells you to fade the clip instead, which you do with its [Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out). Two clips that only touch are fine.

### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes

These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.

The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.

## Good to know

- A clip with no grade set changes nothing, and neither does a qualifier on its own. A qualifier narrows a grade, so there has to be one.
- The [speed](/speed/overview/) commands and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed or left out for an adjustment clip, because it has no source and no picture size.

## With an agent

`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the track and at the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a duration. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.

`set_video` then grades it with everything the Color tab offers, and can also give it point filters directly. To an agent, Strength is the clip's opacity, and `set_action_end` animates it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)

---
title: Qualifiers
description: Limit an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels of one colour or brightness, using hue, saturation and luma ranges.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A qualifier limits an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/)'s grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma. Use it to change one colour and leave the rest of the picture alone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'render_frame']}
  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
/>

<Shot
  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
  alt="The Qualifier section of an adjustment clip, its header reading hue · sat. Hue is ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30°, Soft 15°, and Saturation at Low 0.15, High 1.00, Soft 0.05. Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
/>

## Grade one colour

<Steps>

1. Put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) above the picture, for the span you want.

2. Give it a grade in the **Color** sub-tab. A qualifier on its own changes nothing, because it only narrows a grade.

3. In the **Qualifier** section, press **Pick from Canvas** and click the colour in the preview. Or tick a range and set it by hand.

4. Tick **Show Selection** to see what's picked. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).

5. Adjust the ranges until the selection is clean, then untick **Show Selection**.

</Steps>

A qualifier reaches every track behind the clip. To keep it to one area as well, [add a matte](/color/adjustment-clips/#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).

## The Qualifier section

The **Qualifier** section appears only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip, right after **Adjustment**. A picture clip can't have a qualifier.

It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).

Matching reads the picture behind the clip as it was before the grade, so the grade never changes what it selects.

### The Qualifier summary

The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.

**Reset** appears once anything is set. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.

## Turn a range on

Each range has a checkbox, a strip and three fields. Tick the checkbox and the range starts at its default. That's one undo step named after the range, as unticking it is.

A range that's off has a dimmed strip that ignores presses, and greyed-out fields, so tick it first. Unticking forgets the range's values: tick it again and it's back at its default.

## The three ranges

| Range | Picks pixels by | Strip | Fields | Default when ticked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Hue** | Their colour | The colour spectrum, 0 to 360° | **Centre** 0 to 360°, **Width** 0 to 360°, **Soft** 0 to 180°, in whole degrees | Centre 30°, Width 50°, Soft 25° |
| **Saturation** | How colourful they are | Neutral to fully saturated | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
| **Luma** | How bright they are | Black to white | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |

A number typed outside a field's range is held at the nearest end of it.

### Hue range

**Centre** is the colour, and **Width** is how much of the spectrum around it is fully picked. **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. The default sits on skin tones: 5° to 55° is fully picked, fading to nothing at 340° and 80°.

The band wraps round the spectrum, so a range centred on red picks from both ends of the strip.

Greys are never picked by hue. A colour fades out of a hue range as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, on a scale of 0 to 1.

### Saturation range

This is HSV saturation: 0 is neutral and 1 is fully saturated. **Low** and **High** are the edges of what's fully picked, and **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. At its default the range passes everything, so it does nothing until you narrow it.

Near-black reads as 0, so dark noise doesn't count as colour. A range that starts above 0 leaves near-black pixels out.

### Luma range

This is brightness, from 0 for black to 1 for white, measured as Rec. 709 Y′. Its fields work as Saturation's do, and at its default it passes everything too.

### Low and High never cross

On **Saturation** and **Luma**, a typed **Low** is held at or below **High**, and a typed **High** at or above **Low**. Dragging stops at the same point.

## How ranges combine

A pixel has to fall inside every range that's on. Tick **Hue** and **Luma** and you get that colour at that brightness, not either one.

Each range falls off smoothly across its **Soft** value outside each edge. The partial amounts multiply, so a pixel in the soft edge of two ranges is graded less than one in the soft edge of either. **Soft** at 0 gives a hard edge.

## Use a strip

Each strip is a live picture of its range, and the quickest way to set it.

### Read a strip

A strip shows its own scale: the spectrum for Hue, a neutral to red ramp for Saturation, black to white for Luma. It's dimmed 60 % outside the range and 30 % across the soft bands, so what stays bright is what's fully picked.

The two block knobs mark the range's edges, and the two small squares mark where the softness runs out.

### Drag a strip

| Drag | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| A block knob | On Hue, the **Width**, evenly about the centre. On Saturation and Luma, the **Low** or **High** edge. |
| A small square | **Soft** |
| The band between the knobs | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps round. Saturation and Luma stop at the ends of the scale, keeping their width. |

A press within 5 points of a handle takes it, and knobs are taken before squares. When a range runs to the end of its scale, as Saturation and Luma do at their defaults, the square sits under the knob, so use the **Soft** field or narrow the range first.

A drag is one undo step, named after the range.

### Drag at a tenth of the speed

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move a handle at a tenth of the speed.

### Reset a range

Double-click a strip to put the range back to its default. It stays on. To turn it off, untick it, or right-click the row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Invert

Tick **Invert** to grade everything except what the ranges pick. It's off by default. Use it to desaturate everything but one colour, for example.

## Blur

**Blur** softens the selection, not the picture. On noisy footage a speckled selection turns clean, and the grade blends into its surroundings.

| Control | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Blur** | 0 to 100 %, a slider and a field with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind its chevron | 0 % |

At 100 % the blur is a Gaussian of 24 canvas pixels, and it scales with the canvas, so a Half or Quarter preview blurs the same share of the picture as an export. It's one undo step named **Qualifier Blur**.

Blur never softens a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip, and it does nothing while no range is on.

## Animate a qualifier

An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate a qualifier. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control: the change goes to the action's end, and the numbers ramp there from the clip's own values.

- **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur** ramp smoothly.
- The hue centre takes the short way round the spectrum, so 350° to 10° passes through 0°.
- A range turned on or off, and **Invert**, switch at the action's end.

While an action animates the qualifier, a strip's band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour. The action holds the qualifier as one setting, so changing any row marks them all. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Good to know

- With several adjustment clips selected, the section shows the first clip's values and a badge marks the rows that differ. A change sends the whole range to every selected clip.
- **Invert** with no range on grades nothing, because every pixel counts as picked and Invert takes them all away.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a qualifier only from one adjustment clip to another. A picture clip gets none, and an adjustment clip keeps its own when the attributes come from a picture clip.
- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the ranges are measured on the HLG signal and Luma uses BT.2020's weights, so pick them again after switching a project's dynamic range.

## With an agent

`set_video` sets a qualifier, and can change part of a range and leave the rest as it is. Where the inspector holds a typed number inside its range, an agent's number outside the bounds is turned away. A qualifier on anything but an adjustment clip is an error naming the clip.

`render_frame` can draw the picture [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) shows, for one adjustment clip, and `set_action_end` animates a qualifier. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/)

Where the code differs from the guide or the brief, I followed the code:
- Near-black pixels read as saturation 0, so a saturation range starting at 0 does pick them. The guide says they are never picked.
- The hue guard fades between chroma 0.02 and 0.06, not at a hard 0.06.
- Invert with no range on grades nothing.
- A number typed outside a field's range is held at the nearest end of it.

The Qualifiers page uses the 05h inspector capture, not the window capture. The window capture's preview shows a blue picture under the Selection tag, not the grey selection map, which would contradict the text. That capture may be worth a look when the screens are next refreshed.
